title: Austin Zoning Changes, Beer, and Traffic Debates
summary:
*   Austin City Council approved two requests to rezone residential properties to commercial use, specifically on Cole Avenue and East 7th Street.
*   A restaurant specializing in Assyrian cuisine on Red River was granted a zoning change to allow them to serve beer.
*   Two other residential-to-commercial rezoning requests were postponed. One property on Woodrow/Koenig Lane required a personal inspection by the Council, while a request for West 12th Street was delayed for a traffic study following public protests over increased hazards and preserving the street's beauty.

Mr. Ben King appeared for the property owners stating this property was not suited for
residential, as the rear of the stores facing on Rio Grand would be right next to this
property; and that it was suited for a commercial building and would help the rest of the
neighborhood for residential purposes. MRS. A. E HANCOCK appeared in protest, claiming a
traffic hazard would be increased, and that West 12th was too beautiful to change it to a
commercial district. The Council deferred action on this request until the following
Thursday in order to make a study of the traffic on West 12th Street and work out some way
that traffic could be controlled on this property so it would not add to the existing
hazard.
